scenes.headline: Z-Ordering
scenes.subtitle: Co-locate related data to skip files faster
scenes.narration: Z-ordering is a Delta Lake technique that physically clusters related data so queries read fewer files.

scenes.headline: What Z-ordering does
items: Sorts data by multiple columns using a space-filling curve
Co-locates similar values in the same files
Improves data skipping on filtered queries
scenes.narration: Z-ordering arranges rows so records with similar key values sit together on disk. This lets Delta skip files that cannot match a query filter. The result is dramatically less data scanned for selective queries.

scenes.headline: Applying Z-order
scenes.narration: This command rewrites the table's files and clusters them by product and customer identifiers. Queries filtering on those columns now touch only the relevant files. It is most effective on high-cardinality columns used frequently in WHERE clauses.

scenes.headline: Partitioning vs Z-ordering
scenes.narration: Partitioning splits data into folders and suits a few distinct values like date. Z-ordering works within files and handles high-cardinality filter columns well. The two are complementary rather than competing.

scenes.headline: When and how to use it
items: Choose columns that appear often in query filters
Limit to a few columns; effectiveness drops with many
Re-run OPTIMIZE as new data lands
scenes.narration: Pick the columns users filter on most for maximum skipping. Keep the set small because the benefit dilutes across too many columns. Because new writes arrive unclustered, schedule periodic OPTIMIZE runs.

scenes.text: Z-order the columns you filter by, and let data skipping do the heavy lifting.
scenes.narration: The goal is simple: read the smallest number of files needed to answer each query.
